title: Define SLO tier contracts + customer-facing naming + docs requirements for tiered batching
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
We are standardizing on 3 batching tiers and exposing them across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. This ticket locks:
1) Customer-facing tier names + internal identifiers
2) What each tier *means* (SLO contract / measurement / caveats)
3) Documentation + UX requirements (what we must ship so customers can adopt safely)

Goal
Finalize the tier contracts so Runtime/SRE/DevEx/Console can build against a stable definition, and so beta/GA comms are consistent.

Decision summary (final)
Customer-facing names (docs/UI):
- Fast
- Standard
- Cost-efficient

Internal identifiers (config/API):
- fast
- standard
- cost_efficient

Tier intent
- Fast: lowest p95 latency and best streaming cadence; higher $/token expected.
- Standard: balanced default for most chat/completions.
- Cost-efficient: lower $/token via more aggressive batching/queue delay; accepts higher tail latency; must be coupled with overload protection.

Tier SLO contract (customer-facing)
These are targets for Redwood-managed infrastructure under “typical” workload conditions; they are not per-request guarantees.

Definitions (routes)
- Streaming chat/completions:
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token)
  - Token cadence (inter-token latency) after first token
  - End-to-end time for non-streaming (where applicable)
- Non-streaming completions:
  - End-to-end response latency
- Embeddings/rerank:
  - End-to-end response latency (no streaming)

Measurement and constraints (what we will say in docs)
- Measured at p50/p95/p99 over rolling windows; reported per model, region, and route.
- “Typical workload conditions” for public tier claims:
  - Prompt length: p95 <= ~2k tokens (unless model family is explicitly “long-context optimized”)
  - Output length: <= ~512 tokens for standard claims
  - Cancellation rate below alert threshold (high cancellation can distort queue delay and observed latency)
  - Stable concurrency within documented per-tier envelope (see below)

Targets (initial beta, subject to model-family tuning)
Streaming chat/completions targets (p95):
- Fast: TTFT <= 350ms; steady-state token cadence <= 90ms/token
- Standard: TTFT <= 650ms; steady-state token cadence <= 140ms/token
- Cost-efficient: TTFT <= 1200ms; steady-state token cadence <= 220ms/token

Non-streaming completions targets (p95):
- Fast: <= 1.5s (for typical prompt/output envelope)
- Standard: <= 2.5s
- Cost-efficient: <= 4.5s

Embeddings/rerank targets (p95):
- Fast: <= 300ms
- Standard: <= 500ms
- Cost-efficient: <= 900ms

Concurrency envelope (docs language)
- Fast: optimized for lower to moderate concurrency; will shed load earlier to protect tail latency.
- Standard: broad concurrency range; default recommended tier.
- Cost-efficient: intended for high-throughput batchy workloads; more sensitive to spikes; requires callers to set reasonable timeouts.

Critical caveats / guardrails to document
- Existing explicit batching knobs override tier defaults (tier is a convenience preset, not a lock).
- Tier selection is per route / deployment config (customers can run Fast for user-facing chat and Cost-efficient for offline/batch).
- Streaming workloads: Fast and Standard prioritize token cadence; Cost-efficient may show more “chunking” under load.
- Long-context prompts: tiers may be capped/adjusted by model-family overrides (registry-driven) to avoid OOM / KV cache pressure.
- Overload protection: Cost-efficient must not increase timeout/error rates; load shedding/backpressure reasons should be visible.

Docs + UX requirements (ship-blocking for beta)
Docs must include:
1) "Choosing a batching tier" page: intent, trade-offs, and recommended use cases.
2) Config examples in Python/TS/Go:
   - selecting batching_tier
   - overriding one knob while keeping tier defaults for the rest
3) “Precedence rules” section:
   - explicit knobs > model-family defaults > tier defaults > runtime built-ins
4) “How to validate the tier is working” section:
   - where to see p95, queue delay, batch size distributions
   - what headers/metadata show the effective config (requires runtime explain endpoint)
5) FAQ:
   - impact on streaming cadence
   - what happens during saturation
   - when to override defaults

Console requirements:
- Tier dropdown with short descriptions and warning copy for Cost-efficient.
- Show “Effective batching config” (computed) and highlight overridden fields.
- Link to docs and to “what changed” audit trail for enterprise.

SRE requirements:
- SLOs labeled by tier and route in dashboards.
- Alert thresholds per tier (avoid paging on expected Cost-efficient tail unless it violates tier contract).
- Rollout checklist includes explicit go/no-go metrics and rollback triggers.

Deliverables / artifacts
- Confluence SRE SLO tier doc updated/created: sources/confluence/eng-sre/slo-and-error-budgets/latency-slo-tiers-fast-standard-costefficient.json
- Docs plan aligned with DevEx: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/batching-profiles-docs-plan.json
- Beta release notes include the final naming and opt-in/out language: sources/confluence/product-docs/release-notes/workload-aware-batching-defaults-beta-release.json

Acceptance criteria
- [x] Tier names finalized (customer-facing + internal identifiers) and communicated to Runtime/Console/DevEx.
- [x] SLO contract language drafted and approved by SRE (Sean/Rafael) with clear caveats.
- [x] Docs/UX requirements agreed with DevEx (Alex/Monica/Elliot) including precedence rules and effective-config visibility.
- [x] Review checklist (below) completed and linked in PM-412 launch plan.

Review checklist (must be true before beta cohort enablement)
SRE (Sean Gallagher / Rafael Mendes / Allison Grant):
- [x] Tier targets are measurable with existing/new metrics (TTFT, token cadence, queue delay, batch size).
- [x] Alerts won’t page for expected Cost-efficient behavior; rollback triggers are explicit.
- [x] Error budget policy for tiered SLO labels is documented.

Runtime (Sofia Ivanova / Marcus Reed):
- [x] Config identifiers match exactly: fast|standard|cost_efficient.
- [x] Streaming cadence protections are in place for Fast tier.
- [x] Explicit overrides precedence is implemented and test-covered.

DevEx/Docs (Alex Martinez / Monica Patel / Elliot Price):
- [x] Docs include tier selection examples + override examples.
- [x] Docs include "effective config" debugging guidance.
- [x] Terminology is consistent across docs/SDKs/Console (Cost-efficient; not “eco”).

Product (Aditya Rao / Nikhil Sharma):
- [x] Copy matches pricing/positioning guidance; no implied SLA beyond intended contract.
- [x] Beta cohort messaging aligns with known limitations.
comments: 2025-02-12 (Aditya Rao): Drafted tier naming proposal: Fast / Standard / Cost-efficient. Internal identifier question: cost_efficient vs cost-efficient. Proposing cost_efficient for API stability + common style.
2025-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): SRE asks we avoid hard “SLA” language in docs; phrase as “targets” with workload envelope. Also need explicit token-cadence definition for streaming.
2025-02-17 (Alex Martinez): DevEx request: docs must clearly state precedence rules and show how to inspect effective config; otherwise support load will spike (customers won’t know what’s active).
2025-02-19 (Soojin Lee): Launch messaging: keep “Cost-efficient” (spelled out). Avoid “Eco” as it reads like an environmental claim and confused 2 customers in previous pricing tests.
2025-02-21 (Rafael Mendes): Add concurrency envelope language and ensure Cost-efficient tier is paired with overload protection; otherwise p99 will look scary and trigger false escalations.
2025-02-25 (Aditya Rao): Updated targets table to TTFT + token cadence for streaming + E2E for non-streaming. Marked as initial beta targets subject to per-model tuning (registry overrides).
2025-03-03 (Monica Patel): SDK examples will use batching_tier='standard' as the default in docs; emphasize that setting tier does not break existing explicit batching config.
2025-03-06 (Aditya Rao): Checklist complete. Linked outcomes into PM-412 launch plan and sent summary to eng-runtime + devex + sre channels.
